_readme: PLAIN-ENGLISH DEFINITIONS OF THE TERMS ON THE REPORT SCREENS, for advisors who have
not built one of these before. Mike's request, 2026-09-05: 'most of the accountants
using this will be junior in terms of experience'.
ONE DEFINITION, ONE HOME. A term is defined here and nowhere else, so the wording
cannot drift between the screens that use it. components/base/GlossaryTerm.vue reads
TIER JUDGEMENT, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED (the default-is-mentor-alone ruling of
2026-08-24): this is MENTOR-TIER content and it has no hub screen. The rule that
requires a screen covers content that reaches an AI PROMPT, and none of this does —
it is help text rendered to a person. If a firm ever needs its own wording for a term,
that is a fresh request and this file is already the single source it would cascade
WHAT A DEFINITION IS FOR. It answers 'what is this?' for somebody looking at the box
right now. It is not a training course: two sentences, no jargon inside the
definition, and where a figure is commonly got wrong, say how.
`term` is what the reader sees as the heading of the tooltip. `plain` is the
definition. Both are user-facing and both were put to Mike before they shipped.

collectionProfile.plain: Of everything you invoice in a month, how much of it actually reaches the bank that month, and how much arrives in each of the four months after. It must add to 100%: anything less is money you invoice and never collect.

creditorProfile.plain: Of everything your suppliers bill you in a month, how much you pay that month and how much in each of the four months after. It must add to 100%, for the same reason as the collection profile above it.

openingPosition.plain: The balance sheet the forecast starts from — what the business owns and owes on the day before month one. Every month of the forecast is built on it, so an error here runs through the whole year.

balanceCheck.plain: Total equity less net assets. It should be nil: a balance sheet that balances has no gap. Anything else means a figure is missing, on the wrong side, or entered as a negative.

grossSurplus.plain: Sales less what the goods themselves cost — stock, freight in, commissions. It is the money left to pay the overheads with, before rent, wages or anything else.

overheads.plain: The costs of running the business rather than of the goods sold — wages, rent, power, insurance, depreciation and interest. They are entered as an annual figure and spread evenly across the twelve months.

markup.plain: How much is added to what stock cost to reach the selling price. A 68% mark-up means stock that cost 100 sells for 168. It is not the same as margin, which measures the same gap as a share of the selling price.

bookValue.plain: What an asset is carried at in the accounts today — what it cost, less all the depreciation charged since. It is usually not what the asset would sell for, which is why selling one makes a gain or a loss.

depreciationRate.plain: How much of an asset's value is written off each year. No balance sheet carries it, so it is always yours to set — these start on the platform's own figures and are not the client's.

termLoan.plain: Borrowing repaid on a schedule. Each monthly repayment covers the interest first, and what is left reduces the debt, so the balance falls month by month.

facility.plain: Revolving finance — trade finance, a stock facility, invoice finance. It carries its balance and is charged interest on it, but has no fixed monthly repayment: it is repaid continuously as stock sells, and redrawn as more is bought.

shareholderAccount.plain: Money owed between the company and its owners. In credit, the company owes the shareholder; overdrawn, the shareholder owes the company and is charged interest on it.

workingCapital.plain: Current assets less current liabilities — the cash, stock and debtors a business has to fund its day-to-day trading, after what it owes within the year. Growth consumes it, which is why a profitable business can still run out of money.

gstBasis.plain: Whether the return follows invoices or cash. On the invoice basis GST falls due when you bill; on the cash basis, when the money moves. It changes when GST is paid, never how much.

stockInTransit.term: Stock already paid for, not yet arrived
stockInTransit.plain: Money paid to an overseas supplier for goods still on the water. It is an asset — not yet stock and not yet a cost — until the container lands, and it carries no GST until it does.

provenance.plain: Every figure is tagged: read from the file you dropped, entered by a person, or seeded from last year's actuals as a starting point. A seeded figure is a starting point for a judgement, never a forecast.
